 These Appeals, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 -4-
 Nc: 2023:Khc-D:8837
 Mfa No. 20879 of 2011
 C/W Mfa No. 20880 of 2011
 Judgment

The appeal in MFA No.20879/2011 and MFA No.20880/2011 are filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 26.08.2010 passed by the MACT-III, Bellary in MVC No.782/2007 and MVC No.781/2007 questioning the liability fixed on the insurance company.
2. The fact of occurrence of accident and injury sustained by the claimants in the said accident is not in dispute.
The applicability and coverage of the insurance policy is also not in dispute.
The appellant-Insurance Company is before this Court only challenging the liability fastened on it in both the appeals.

3. Heard the learned counsel for parties and perused the material available on record.
4.

In the present case, it is submitted that both claimants have traveled in the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-35/4832 as a fair paid passenger and met with NC: 2023:KHC-D:8837 accident and due to that the claimants have sustained the injuries.
Hence, the claim petition is filed.
The Tribunal awarded compensation and fastened the liability on both owner and insurer of the auto rickshaw jointly and severally.
5. It is the contention urged by the counsel for the appellant in both the appeals that the auto rickshaw is a light motor vehicle (Transport).
But, the driver was having driving license to drive only light motor vehicle (non- transport).
Therefore, submitted that the driver was not holding valid and effective driving license and hence, contended that there is breach of policy conditions.

Hence,
insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

6. The issue involved is no more res intergra in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Limited Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited1.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Limited Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is held in the said judgment that the person who is holding (2017) 14 SCC 663, NC:
2023:KHC-D:8837 the driving license to drive light motor vehicle (Non- transport) is also competent to drive light motor vehicle (transport), even though there is no endorsement as (transport).
Therefore, issue involved is squarely covered by the Judgment of Mukund Dewangan's (supra) case.
Therefore, tribunal is correct in saddling the liability on the Insurance Company.

Accordingly, I pass the following :
